subject: OmniFin deployment readiness — SLOs, topology, and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@omnifin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: OmniFin — deployment readiness & SLO alignment

Hi Taylor — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Pain points you confirmed
- High variability in live traffic (burst-y business hours) causing latency spikes and retries.
- Cost sensitivity: must keep inference spend predictable under a committed monthly budget.
- Compliance: data residency + audit logs required for production.

Goals we heard
- Deliver interactive LLM features with P95 latency <= 150ms for 95% of requests; acceptable brief bursts up to 250–320 concurrent inflight requests with degraded but usable latency.
- Keep per-token unit economics within procurement target (we discussed model/quantization tradeoffs).
- Production rollout inside US East region, private data plane (VPC) preferred.

Technical summary / model requirements
- Primary model family: large open models (70B-class) or a 30B fallback variant. You indicated preference for a mix of quality and cost; quantized INT8 routes are acceptable if we preserve accuracy for your top-10 prompt templates.
- Typical prompt length: ~40–80 tokens; average response ~60 tokens.
- Steady-state QPS estimate you gave: ~120 QPS; peak bursts up to ~320 QPS lasting ~60–120s.

Suggested topology for PoC
- Redwood Dedicated pool in us-east with autoscaling policy: base capacity to handle steady state (4 gpus) + burst autoscale up to 8 gpus for short spikes.
- Enable prefix/KV cache for common prompts and warmup instances during predicted peak windows.
- Routing policy: primary to dedicated cluster; fallback to a smaller hosted variant during cold starts or degraded capacity.

SLO targets (for discussion)
- P95 latency target: 150ms (token-level pipeline optimizations and batching enabled).
- Tail latency escape clause: allow up to 10% of requests to exceed P95 during peaks but maintain success rate >= 99.5%.

Attachments: omnifin-internal-requirements.xlsx (sheet: throughput_and_prompts)

Immediate next steps (action owners)
- Alex: share topology diagram + draft PoC scope (attached link) by EOD tomorrow.
- Taylor: confirm any hard constraints on model family or required accuracy metrics.
- Marissa: I'll connect you to commercial for pricing baseline.
- Schedule: Technical deep-dive w/ infra + procurement on 2026-07-14 — Alex to send invite.

If anything above is off, flag it and I will update.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

Taylor — great questions. Short answers + specifics for the deep-dive:

1) Caching recommendation
- Use a hybrid approach: router-side (edge) caching for exact-match templates and prefix-caching inside the GPU runtime for KV reuse. Router cache eliminates unnecessary request traffic; runtime cache speeds up autoregressive token generation when many sessions reuse history. We'll include recommended TTLs in the topology doc.

2) Cost delta (ballpark)
- 70B (non-quantized) serving path: ~2.5–3x cost per token vs a 30B non-quantized baseline.
- Mixed 70B + 30B routing with quantized INT8 variants can reduce unit cost ~35–50% for routable queries, depending on hit rate and cache effectiveness. We'll model three scenarios in the commercial worksheet.

Operational notes
- Warmup strategy: scheduled instance warmups for known peak windows + aggressive prefix cache for unpredictable spikes.
- Token length assumptions: we will conservatively size KV cache and batch windows around 120-token sequences to avoid tail blowups.

I attached a draft PoC proposal and a link to a topology diagram for the deep-dive call.
